items.label: FIGURE B1.4.1
items.title: Societal poverty line
items.content: The figure contains two panels: a. Global poverty trends and b. Share of global poor by region, 2022. Panel a is a line chart showing poverty rate (%) on the y-axis from 0 to 80, and years on the x-axis from 1990 to 2020. It plots four lines: $2.15 (red), $3.65 (yellow), $6.85 (black), and Societal poverty line (green). All lines show a downward trend over time. Panel b is a stacked horizontal bar chart showing the share of global poor (%) by region for four poverty lines: $2.15, $3.65, $6.85, and SPL. The regions are East Asia and Pacific, Europe and Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, Middle East and North Africa, South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Rest of the world. Source: World Bank, Poverty and Inequality Platform (PIP, version September 2024), https://pip.worldbank.org. Note: SPL = societal poverty line. The poverty lines of $2.15, $3.65, $6.85, and the SPL are per person per day (expressed in 2017 purchasing power parity dollars).
